# The board-smoothing sheet: what each frame is, and what each candidate cost.
#
# Generated by tools/capture-smoothing-sheet.ps1 from content/map.txt, read through
# HexMap.ParseUtf8 like any other map. Every frame is the same board: the cells, the
# corridor and the level of every cell are untouched, so anything that differs between
# two frames is the ground's surface and nothing that differs is the playfield.

board
    cells        247 (19 by 13)
    corridor     51 cells
    boundaries   268 edges between two cells of different level -- the edges each candidate smooths
    cliff posts  0 drawn under the board today
    steepest     corridor cell 4,4 (column,row), level d -- the corridor cell with the most height change around it; check-*.png crops it

cameras
    match        the shipped framing: yaw 0, pitch 35.26, field of view 40, framed on the floor as OrbitCameraRig.Reframe does
    plan         straight down, orthographic, the board fitted with the shipped margin -- render-map.ps1's view, which has no Unity camera of its own
    frame        1600x900; sheets hold each frame at half size; checks hold a 240px crop at 2x

sheet layout (both cameras, both checks), read left to right, top to bottom
    today            skin-plain       pieces-plain
    skin-contour     skin-band        skin-both
    pieces-contour   pieces-band      pieces-both

skin
    what         one mesh over the whole board: a flat plateau per ground cell at 0.60 of the hex, planar slopes between plateaus, the pack's road pieces left standing and met at their own edge heights
    meshes       1 (plus the 51 road tiles it runs up to)
    vertices     16518, triangles 5506, flat shaded
    map change   nothing to author: the mesh is regenerated from the map at scene-build time
    cliff posts  gone; the rim banks down by the dressing's rim drop and hangs a skirt of earth
    scenery      stands where it stood; a prop placed off a cell's centre can sit on a slope

pieces
    what         one tile per cell: a ground cell lifts the corners it shares with a neighbour one level up to that neighbour's height, so the slope lives in the lower cell and the higher cell stays flat, as the pack's own ramp does; two levels or more is left as a cliff
    tiles        196 ground tiles: 50 wear the pack's flat grass tile unchanged, 146 are authored pieces
    patterns     13 distinct authored pieces on this board (a pattern is the six corner lifts in quarter levels, rotations counted once); the pack ships three of the shapes a board can need (flat, half slope, full slope), none of the corner cases
    vertices     3444, triangles 1148 across the authored pieces
    walls        14 cell edges where a wall still shows between two cells (a step of two levels or more, or a road the ground could not meet)
    map change   generated here, so nothing; hand-authored in the pack's style it is one model per new pattern, and a new map can introduce patterns this one never does
    cliff posts  gone between cells; the rim keeps the tile's own metre of body
    the pieces   000000 000222 002222 000022 -2-20000 -2-2-2-2-20 000002 022222 -2-2-2000 222222 022022 -222200 002202

aids
    contour      a dark ribbon 0.10 m wide along every edge between two cells of different level, laid on the candidate's own surface; 268 edges on this board
    band         one tint per level over the atlas, walking blue to green to yellow to orange from the lowest level in use to the highest, on ground and road alike; the slope between two plateaus changes colour at the cell boundary
